summary: Theorem 4.4 is false under its stated global step-size conditions: a finite two-state MDP with fixed stationary uniform behavior visits all four state-action pairs infinitely often but the learned greedy policy is suboptimal forever. Exact reachability iteration remains supportable. Local released PER weighting, numerical interpretation, Circle safety specification and README dispatch problems are Minor; historical empirical effects remain unresolved.
limitations: No author code, training, model or benchmark execution was performed; finite diagnostics are reviewer-owned.
Separate OpenReview supplementary attachment returned 403; the full embedded appendix was inspected.
No raw experiment logs, SWU aggregation script or publication-time configuration binding was located in the preserved source.
PyTorch was not available in the checked Windows Python or isolated runtime. Broadcasting was verified by static shapes, primary documentation and scalar algebra, without a tensor-library execution.
No complete repaired asynchronous reachability convergence theorem or empirical repair is certified.
No exhaustive later-version/erratum audit or first-discovery claim.
No actual conversation URL, independently observed UI model label, auxiliary-agent model identifier or accessible Space reference was exposed.

problems.title: Global step-size assumptions do not imply sampled optimal convergence
problems.claim_location: Theorem 4.4, PDF pages 4-5; Equations 11,13,14; Appendix B.4 pages 14-16
problems.assumptions: Finite states x,y with two actions g,b, deterministic alternation under both; gamma=1/2, rho concentrated at x; unsafe set empty (allowed). Reward r(x,g)=1, all others zero. Fixed stationary uniform independent behavior; all four pairs have limiting frequency 1/4 almost surely. psi0=0; Q0(x,b)=1/2 and others zero; no zero-Q initialization requirement. beta_2n=2^(-(n+5)), beta_(2n+1)=1/(n+2).
problems.check: Global step sum diverges, square sum=1/768+pi^2/6-1 is finite and beta tends to zero. Total step weight at x is only1/16. All safety values remain0; masks are full and kappa-gap condition is vacuous. Q in[0,2] invariant; Q(x,g)<=1/8 while Q(x,b)>=15/32 on every sample path. True Q values are4/3,1/3 at x and2/3 at y.
problems.result: Learned greedy policy chooses bad action at x forever, with reward value0 versus optimal safe4/3; both value and policy convergence claims fail. Reviewer-owned 2000-step seed230 diagnostic illustrates Qx=(.0561212,.4971123), but proof is analytic.
problems.counterevidence: Behavior is fixed stationary and all pair frequencies positive, eliminating nonstationary/rare-visit objections. Step sequence is not nonincreasing, but monotonicity is not stated. Standard per-visit schedules would exclude the example. Exact reachability theorem and empirical curves are not refuted by it.
problems.impact: Directly refutes the central advertised convergence guarantee; Major independently of repair difficulty or empirical score change.
problems.correction: Require per-pair divergent cumulative step sizes and appropriate asynchronous convergence assumptions/proof. This necessary repair excludes the example; full general SA-REF repair is not verified.
problems.repair_verification: Require per-pair divergent cumulative step sizes and appropriate asynchronous convergence assumptions/proof. This necessary repair excludes the example; full general SA-REF repair is not verified.

problems.title: Classic-control importance weighting broadcasts over the batch
problems.claim_location: Paper Section5.2 and Algorithm1; utils_classic_control.py61,70-73; replay_buffer.py146-150,177-187; algos/sp2dqn.py197-216 and sp3dqn.py199-218
problems.assumptions: Safety residuals have shape(B,1); sampled weights have shape(B), with B>1 and nonconstant valid weights. Example current values(.30,.80), targets(.05,.05) yield residuals(.25,.75) in admissible bounds.
problems.check: Broadcast multiplication yields(B,B), loss mean(e_i^2)*mean(w_j) rather than mean(w_i*e_i^2). For e=(1/4,3/4),w=(1,1/2), actual loss15/64 versus11/64; gradients(3/16,9/16) versus(1/4,3/8). Static shapes and primary PyTorch documentation checked; scalar arithmetic independently executed.
problems.result: Individual importance correction disappears, leaving a common batch scale. Optional SP3 Q weighting also affected.
problems.counterevidence: Prioritized sampling remains. Highway branch explicitly squeezes residuals and is unaffected. No publication-time code binding or benchmark impact demonstrated. Actual tensor library diagnostic unavailable in checked runtimes.
problems.impact: Supported local implementation error in release; impact on central published empirical conclusions unresolved, so Minor.
problems.correction: Reshape weights to(B,1) or squeeze residuals to(B); local algebra verified, no full author training or empirical repair.
problems.repair_verification: Reshape weights to(B,1) or squeeze residuals to(B); local algebra verified, no full author training or empirical repair.

problems.title: Numerical summaries and blanket dominance contradict the tables
problems.claim_location: PDF page8 Section6.2 and page20 AppendixC3.1; Tables1,4,5
problems.assumptions: Compare printed conditions and means; no statistical-significance inference from small differences.
problems.check: Table1 proposed row means .975,.738333 support .98,.74, not prose .90,.79. Table4 has .95,.73. TwoWay favors PER(.98>.88), Merge favors SPOM(.95>.94). TwoWay reward10.124/10.520 is below SafeQ10.636; SPOM Roundabout crash.167 exceeds SafeQ.090.
problems.result: Overall numerical prose, named winners and across-all-metrics dominance are incorrect.
problems.counterevidence: Overall first/second SWU ordering survives. Table1 versusTable4 Roundabout differences are explained by comparison-set minimum target changing from.055 to.047; not an independent contradiction.
problems.impact: Local reporting/interpretation defect without demonstrated collapse of overall empirical advantage.
problems.correction: Use table-supported summaries and explicit reward/safety tradeoffs. No corrected raw aggregate or significance claim.
problems.repair_verification: Use table-supported summaries and explicit reward/safety tradeoffs. No corrected raw aggregate or significance claim.

problems.title: Circle unsafe-set inequality reverses the stated safety classification
problems.assumptions: x_max=2.5; intended constraint is to remain inside the two walls.
problems.check: Printed S_u={abs(x)<=2.5} labels x0 unsafe and x3 safe; released cost/termination uses abs(x)>2.5.
problems.result: Displayed benchmark formula reverses cost and reward/termination classification if implemented literally.
problems.counterevidence: Released code agrees with inside-safe prose, so actual experimental inversion is not established. Crash reward differs between paper(-1) and current config(-10), with historical settings unknown.
problems.impact: Local essential environment specification error; Minor with bounded empirical consequence.
problems.correction: For the stated/source environment use S_u={abs(x)>2.5}; boundary at equality is safe. This classification is verified; historical complete environment repair not claimed.
problems.repair_verification: For the stated/source environment use S_u={abs(x)>2.5}; boundary at equality is safe. This classification is verified; historical complete environment repair not claimed.

problems.title: README Circle command selects a reward-shaping baseline
problems.assumptions: Run the advertised bare entrypoint with preserved defaults, no unstated file changes.
problems.check: Default algo is priorrewsdqn and the entrypoint dispatches to PriorRewsDQN. Its main block does not parse overrides. README claims the command is SPOM_PER.
problems.result: Advertised command and actual static method identity disagree.
problems.counterevidence: README Merge command explicitly selects sp_perdqn and is consistent. Historical publication commands remain unknown.
problems.impact: Current-release reproduction defect, not evidence that original experiments used the wrong method.
problems.correction: Provide correct explicit configuration/launch mapping; no full author-code launch performed or certified.
problems.repair_verification: Provide correct explicit configuration/launch mapping; no full author-code launch performed or certified.
